decisions.reason: The accent already must derive literally from the exact approved Option 2 Hero V geometry, so restoring and fixing that geometry does not change this Requirement's state.
Message 140 already directly introduces the locked-asset policy and records the altered-geometry failure; no additional or incomplete candidate Event requires correction.
The candidate already has a message-140 MODIFY stating that the approved Hero V remains fixed while the accent is adapted to preserve the shared peak horizon.
The closing V is already required to derive from the exact approved Option 2 Hero V, so reinstating that fixed reference leaves its construction requirements unchanged.
The source requires surrounding type to accommodate the fixed Hero V but does not change the established architectural E/L construction or terminal constraints.
Restoring the Hero V does not alter the relational rule that the second V sits above E/L but below the Hero V and É accent.
Pausing further wordmark refinement until the Hero V is restored does not change the existing cohesive-reading goal for kerning and rhythm.
The Hero V geometry correction does not change the deferred champagne-metal material direction or its application constraint.
The source addresses Hero V geometry and adaptation of surrounding forms, not the selected all-caps case treatment.
Review-image file accessibility is unrelated to the decision to restore and preserve the approved Hero V geometry.
